title: Chimichurri steak
summary: Juicy grilled steak sliced against the grain and topped with punchy parsley, garlic and red-wine-vinegar chimichurri.
ingredients: 700 g beef steak, such as rump, about 3 cm thick
1 bunch parsley, leaves picked and finely chopped
method: Mix the parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, 60 ml olive oil, oregano, chilli flakes and half the salt. Leave for 20 minutes so the flavours blend.
Pat the steak dry and rub with the remaining salt and the pepper. Rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat for 2–3 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining olive oil.
Cook the steak for 4–5 minutes without moving it, until deeply browned. Turn and cook 3–4 minutes more for medium-rare, still pink in the middle.
Rest the steak under foil for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Spoon the chimichurri over the steak and serve with the resting juices.

stages.title: Make the chimichurri
steps: Combine the chopped parsley and garlic in a bowl with the red wine vinegar, 60 ml of the olive oil, the dried oregano, the chilli flakes and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Stir well, then leave at room temperature for 20 minutes so the garlic mellows and the flavours blend.

stages.title: Season the steak
steps: Pat the steak dry with paper towel so it browns rather than steams.
Rub the steak all over with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the black pepper.
Leave the steak at room temperature for 15 minutes while the chimichurri sits.

stages.title: Cook the steak
steps: Heat a heavy frying pan or chargrill pan over high heat for 2–3 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Cook the steak for 4–5 minutes on one side without moving it, until deeply browned.
Turn and cook for another 3–4 minutes for medium-rare, until browned outside and still pink in the middle. Cook longer if you prefer it more done.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Move the steak to a board and rest it, loosely covered with foil, for 10 minutes.
Slice the steak across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Spoon the chimichurri over the sliced steak and serve with the resting juices.

tips: Pat the steak dry before seasoning, because surface moisture stops a crust forming in the hot pan.
Resting the steak for 10 minutes lets the juices settle back into the meat, so they don't run out when you slice.
Chop the parsley by hand rather than blending it, as a food processor bruises the leaves and makes a muddy, pasty sauce.
Slicing across the grain shortens the muscle fibres, which makes rump tender to chew.
variations: Replace half the parsley with coriander for a brighter, more citrusy sauce.
Add 1 finely chopped red onion to the chimichurri for extra sharpness and crunch.
storage: Refrigerate the steak and chimichurri separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Eat the steak cold in sandwiches or salads, or reheat gently in a pan for 1–2 minutes so it doesn't overcook.

title: Focaccia
summary: Fluffy olive-oil bread with a crisp golden crust, rosemary and flaky sea salt.
method: Mix the bread flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 1 tbsp olive oil in a large bowl for 2–3 minutes, until no dry flour remains and the dough is very sticky.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes. Fold the dough over itself all the way around, rest 30 minutes, then fold again and rest 30 minutes more, until puffy and bubbly.
Spread 2 tbsp olive oil in a 20 x 30 cm tray, tip in the dough and stretch it towards the corners. Cover and rest 40 minutes, until doubled and airy.
About 15 minutes before the rise ends, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Drizzle with the remaining olive oil, press deep dimples all over with oiled fingertips, then scatter over the rosemary and flaky sea salt.
Bake for 22–25 minutes, until deep golden and the base is crisp. Rest in the tray 5 minutes, then cool on a wire rack 5 minutes and cut.

stages.title: Mix the dough
steps: In a large bowl, combine the bread flour, instant yeast and the 10 g salt.
Pour in the warm water and 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Mix with a wet hand or spoon for 2–3 minutes, until no dry flour remains and the dough is very sticky.

stages.title: Rest and fold
steps: Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel and rest for 30 minutes.
With a wet hand, lift one edge of the dough and fold it over to the middle. Turn the bowl and repeat 8 times around the dough, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Fold the dough the same way again, cover and rest for a further 30 minutes, until puffy and bubbly. That makes 2 sets of folds and 90 minutes in total.

stages.title: Second rise in the tray
steps: Pour 2 tbsp of the olive oil into a 20 x 30 cm baking tray and spread it over the base and sides.
Tip the dough into the tray and turn it once to coat in oil. Gently stretch it towards the corners, stopping if it springs back.
Cover and leave in a warm spot for 40 minutes, until doubled in size, airy and jiggly.
About 15 minutes before the end of the rise, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).

stages.title: Dimple and bake
steps: Drizzle the remaining 1/2 tbsp olive oil over the dough and oil your fingertips.
Press your fingertips straight down to the base of the tray all over the dough to make deep dimples.
Scatter over the rosemary leaves and the flaky sea salt.
Bake on the middle shelf for 22–25 minutes, until deep golden on top and the base is crisp and sounds hollow when tapped.

stages.title: Cool
steps: Leave the focaccia in the tray for 5 minutes, then slide it onto a wire rack.
Cool for 5 minutes more, then cut into squares and serve warm.

tips: A wet, sticky dough traps more steam, which gives the open, airy crumb, so resist adding extra flour.
Folding the dough builds strength without kneading, so it holds its bubbles.
Pressing the dimples right to the tray lets oil pool in them and crisps the base.
Use warm water, not hot, as hot water can kill the yeast.
variations: Press halved cherry tomatoes and pitted kalamata olives into the dimples before baking.
Replace the rosemary with thyme leaves and thinly sliced garlic, adding the garlic just before baking so it doesn't burn.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days. Freeze sliced pieces for up to 2 months and reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until warmed through and crisp.

title: Bún chả
summary: Caramelised pork patties with rice vermicelli, fresh herbs and a tangy fish-sauce dipping broth.
method: Mix the pork mince with half the garlic, the spring onions, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and the black pepper until sticky. Shape into 16 small patties and chill for 30 minutes.
Cut one carrot into matchsticks and slice the other into rounds. Dissolve the remaining sugar in 250 ml warm water, then add the remaining fish sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar and remaining garlic.
Add the chilli and carrot rounds to the broth and leave to pickle while you cook.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the patties in two batches, 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and no longer pink in the centre, then add them to the broth.
Cook the rice vermicelli to the packet directions, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Serve the noodles with torn lettuce, mint leaves and carrot matchsticks on a platter, with the patties in broth alongside.

stages.title: Marinate the pork
steps: Finely chop the garlic and thinly slice the spring onions.
In a bowl, combine the pork mince, half the garlic, the spring onions, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Mix well with your hands for about 1 minute, until sticky.
Shape the mixture into 16 small flat patties, about 5 cm wide.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes so the flavours soak in and the patties hold their shape.

stages.title: Make the dipping broth
steps: Cut one carrot into thin matchsticks and slice the other into thin rounds. Keep the matchsticks for serving.
In a bowl, stir the remaining 2 tbsp sugar into 250 ml warm water for about 1 minute, until completely dissolved.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp fish sauce, the juice of the 2 limes, the rice vinegar and the remaining garlic.
Stir the sliced red chilli and the carrot rounds into the broth and set aside to pickle lightly while you cook.

stages.title: Cook the patties
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook half the patties for 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Transfer the cooked patties to a plate, then cook the remaining patties over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and no longer pink in the centre.
Add the patties to the dipping broth.

stages.title: Prepare the noodles and herbs
steps: Cook the rice vermicelli according to the packet, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Pick the mint leaves and tear the lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Arrange the noodles, lettuce, mint and carrot matchsticks on a platter.

tips: Resting the patties in the fridge lets the fish sauce and sugar season the pork and helps the patties hold together in the pan.
Cook in batches so the pan stays hot; crowding steams the pork and stops it browning and caramelising.
Dissolve the sugar fully in warm water before adding the fish sauce and lime, so the broth is balanced and not gritty.
variations: Add thin slices of pork shoulder marinated in the same mix and cook them for 2–3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Cook the patties on a barbecue grill over medium-high heat for the same time for a smokier flavour.
storage: Store patties, broth, noodles and herbs separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat the patties in a pan over medium heat until hot through and serve with cold noodles.

title: Gulab jamun
summary: Soft milk-solid dumplings soaked in fragrant cardamom and rose syrup until tender and glossy.
method: Lightly crush the cardamom. Simmer the sugar, 300 ml water and cardamom in a saucepan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until slightly sticky but still runny. Stir in the rosewater and keep warm on low.
Whisk the milk powder, flour and baking powder, then rub in the butter until it looks like fine crumbs. Add the milk gradually to form a soft, slightly tacky dough and rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Lightly oil your palms with a little of the vegetable oil. Divide the dough into 16 pieces and roll each into a smooth ball with no cracks.

Heat the rest of the oil in a deep saucepan over low-medium heat to about 140°C. Fry the balls in batches for 8–10 minutes, until deep golden and puffed, with a skewer coming out clean from the centre.
Drain the balls briefly on paper towel, then add them to the warm syrup. Soak off the heat for at least 30 minutes, until swollen and soft through, then serve 4 per person.

stages.title: Make the syrup
steps: Lightly crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife.
Combine the white sugar, 300 ml water and the cardamom in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until the syrup is slightly sticky but still runs freely from a spoon.
Stir in the rosewater, then turn the heat to the lowest setting to keep the syrup warm.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Whisk the milk powder, plain flour and baking powder in a large bowl until evenly combined.
Rub the butter into the dry ingredients with your fingertips until the mixture looks like fine crumbs.
Add the milk 1 tablespoon at a time, bringing the mixture together gently into a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Rest the dough, covered, for 10 minutes so the milk powder hydrates.

stages.title: Shape the balls
steps: Lightly grease your palms with a little of the vegetable oil.
Divide the dough into 16 equal pieces.
Roll each piece between your palms into a smooth ball with no cracks, as cracks open up when frying.

stages.title: Fry the gulab jamun
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-based saucepan over low-medium heat until it reaches about 140°C, or until a small piece of dough sinks and rises slowly with gentle bubbles.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time, gently swirling the oil around them, for 8–10 minutes, until deep golden brown all over and puffed.
Test one ball: it should feel light and firm, and a skewer pushed into the centre should come out clean with no raw dough.
Lift the balls out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towel for 30 seconds. Repeat with the remaining balls.

stages.title: Soak in syrup
steps: Make sure the syrup is warm, not boiling hot, then add the fried balls to it.
Leave the balls to soak off the heat for at least 30 minutes, until they swell and are soft right through.
Serve 4 balls per person, warm or at room temperature, with some syrup spooned over.

tips: Keep the oil at about 140°C so the centres cook through before the outsides darken; hotter oil gives a dark shell and a raw middle.
Add the milk gradually, as milk powder brands absorb differently. A dough that is too wet spreads and splits when frying.
Add the balls to warm syrup, not hot syrup, so they absorb it evenly instead of shrinking and going tough.
Knead the dough only until it comes together; overworking makes the gulab jamun dense and chewy.
variations: Press a flaked almond or a few pistachio slivers into the centre of each ball before rolling.
Replace the rosewater with a pinch of saffron threads steeped in the warm syrup.
storage: Refrigerate in the syrup in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Warm gently in the microwave in 20-second bursts, or serve cold.

title: Dorayaki
summary: Fluffy golden pancake sandwiches filled with sweet red bean paste, a classic Japanese treat.
method: Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and honey for 2–3 minutes until pale, thick and foamy. Whisk in the water, then sift in the flour and baking powder and fold until just smooth.
Cover and rest the batter for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, divide the red bean paste into 4 portions and shape each into a flat disc about 6 cm wide.
Heat a large non-stick pan over low–medium heat and wipe with a little vegetable oil. Cook 3 tbsp batter rounds for 2–3 minutes until bubbles form and edges look set.
Flip and cook 1 minute until golden and springy. Cool on a wire rack, repeating to make 8 pancakes, re-oiling the pan lightly between batches.
Cool the pancakes for 3–4 minutes. Spread a bean paste disc on the paler side of one pancake, leaving a 1 cm border, then top with another pancake, golden side up, pressing the edges together.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and honey in a large bowl for 2–3 minutes until pale, thick and slightly foamy.
Add the water and whisk until the honey has dissolved.
Sift the plain flour and baking powder over the egg mixture and fold gently until just smooth, with no dry flour left.
The batter should fall from the whisk in a thick ribbon; if it is stiff, add 1 tbsp more water.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the bowl and rest the batter for 20 minutes so the flour hydrates and the pancakes cook up tender.
Meanwhile, divide the red bean paste into 4 portions and loosely shape each into a flat disc about 6 cm wide.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan over low–medium heat for 2 minutes. Wipe it with a little of the vegetable oil on a paper towel, leaving only a thin film.
Pour 3 tbsp batter into the pan to form a round about 8 cm wide. Cook 3 at a time for 2–3 minutes, until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more, until the underside is golden and the pancake springs back when pressed. Transfer to a wire rack.
Repeat with the remaining batter to make 8 pancakes, re-oiling the pan lightly between batches and adjusting the heat if they colour too quickly.

stages.title: Fill and serve
steps: Let the pancakes cool for 3–4 minutes so the bean paste doesn't melt.
Spread a portion of red bean paste over the paler side of a pancake, leaving a 1 cm border.
Top with a second pancake, golden side up, and press the edges gently together. Repeat to make 4 dorayaki.

tips: Resting the batter lets the flour absorb the liquid, giving a softer, more even crumb.
Low–medium heat gives an evenly golden surface; a hotter pan browns the outside before the centre cooks.
Cooking the pancakes in a thin film of oil, wiped almost dry, gives the smooth tan finish dorayaki are known for.
variations: Fill with sweetened chestnut paste instead of red bean paste.
Spread the pancakes with a thin layer of lightly whipped cream before adding the bean paste.
storage: Wrap each dorayaki in plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature or warm for 10 seconds in the microwave before eating.

title: Key lime pie
summary: Tangy lime custard in a buttery biscuit crust topped with softly whipped cream.
method: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan). Blitz the digestive biscuits to fine crumbs, mix with the melted butter and press into a 20 cm pie dish.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, until lightly golden at the edges and firm to touch. Keep the oven on.
Whisk the egg yolks for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thick. Whisk in the condensed milk, lime juice and lime zest, then pour into the warm crust.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles slightly. Cool in the dish for 30 minutes.
Cover and chill for 3 hours or overnight, until firm in the centre. Chill the cream bowl for the last 15 minutes.
Whisk the thickened cream and icing sugar in the chilled bowl until soft peaks form, about 2–3 minutes. Spread over the pie and serve cold.

stages.title: Make the biscuit crust
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan).
Blitz the digestive biscuits in a food processor to fine crumbs, or crush them in a zip-lock bag with a rolling pin.
Mix the crumbs with the melted butter until they look like damp sand.
Press the mixture firmly over the base and up the sides of a 20 cm pie dish, using the back of a glass to compact it.

stages.title: Bake the crust
steps: Bake the crust for 10 minutes, until lightly golden at the edges and firm to touch.
Remove from the oven and leave on a rack while you make the filling. Keep the oven on.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thick. Use pasteurised eggs if serving young children, pregnant or elderly people, as the filling is only lightly baked.
Whisk in the condensed milk until smooth.
Add the lime juice and lime zest and whisk until combined; the mixture will thicken slightly.
Pour the filling into the warm crust.

stages.title: Bake the filling
steps: Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles slightly when the dish is gently shaken.
Cool the pie in the dish on a rack for 30 minutes before chilling.

stages.title: Cool and chill the pie
steps: Cool the pie on the rack for 30 minutes, until no longer warm to touch, then cover loosely with plastic wrap.
Refrigerate for 3 hours, or overnight, until completely firm in the centre.
Put the bowl you will use for the cream in the fridge for the last 15 minutes.

stages.title: Whip the cream and serve
steps: Whisk the thickened cream and icing sugar in the chilled bowl until soft peaks form, about 2–3 minutes.
Spread or pipe the cream over the chilled pie.
Cut with a hot, dry knife, wiping the blade between slices, and serve cold.

tips: Whisking the yolks before adding the condensed milk gives a smoother, silkier filling.
Baking the filling only until the centre still wobbles means it finishes setting as it chills, so it stays creamy instead of turning rubbery.
Pressing the crumbs firmly with a glass stops the crust crumbling when you cut the slices.
Cutting with a hot, dry knife gives clean slices through the set filling.
variations: Replace the lime juice and zest with lemon for a lemon condensed milk pie.
Use gingernut biscuits instead of digestives for a spicier crust.
storage: Refrigerate, covered, for up to 3 days. Serve cold. Freezing is not recommended as the cream topping becomes watery.

title: Swedish cinnamon buns
summary: Soft cardamom-scented buns spiralled with buttery cinnamon sugar and finished with pearl sugar.
method: Warm the milk and 50 g of the butter in a saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, until the butter melts and the milk is lukewarm.
Mix the flour, 50 g of the caster sugar, yeast, cardamom and salt, add the milk mixture and knead 8–10 minutes until smooth. Rise covered in a warm spot for 1 hour, until doubled.
Mix 50 g soft butter, the remaining 40 g caster sugar and the cinnamon into a paste. Roll the dough into a 30 x 40 cm rectangle, spread with the paste, roll up and slice into 12 rounds.
Place the buns cut side up on two lined trays, cover and rest in a warm spot for 30 minutes, until puffy. Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) for the last 15 minutes.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake for 10–12 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden and hollow-sounding underneath.
Brush with the remaining 30 g melted butter, sprinkle with the white sugar and cool on the trays for 10 minutes.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Warm the milk and 50 g of the butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, until the butter melts and the milk is lukewarm, not hot. Remove from the heat.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, 50 g of the caster sugar, the dried yeast, ground cardamom and salt.
Pour in the milk mixture and stir to form a shaggy dough.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 8–10 minutes, until smooth, elastic and slightly tacky.

stages.title: First rise
steps: Place the dough in a clean large bowl and cover with a tea towel.
Leave in a warm spot for 1 hour, until doubled in size.

stages.title: Fill and shape
steps: Mix 50 g of the soft butter, the remaining 40 g caster sugar and the ground cinnamon into a smooth paste.
Roll the dough on a floured bench into a 30 x 40 cm rectangle.
Spread the cinnamon paste evenly over the dough, leaving a 1 cm border along one long edge.
Roll up tightly from the opposite long edge, finishing at the clean border, then slice into 12 even rounds.
Place the buns cut side up on two baking trays lined with baking paper, spaced apart.

stages.title: Second rise
steps: Cover the trays loosely with tea towels and leave in a warm spot for 30 minutes, until puffy and springy when pressed gently.
In the last 15 minutes, heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).

stages.title: Bake and finish
steps: Beat the egg and brush it over the buns.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden and the buns sound hollow when tapped underneath.
Melt the remaining 30 g butter and brush it over the hot buns, then sprinkle with the white sugar.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes before serving.

tips: Heat the milk only until lukewarm, because hot milk kills the yeast and the dough won't rise.
Keep the dough slightly tacky, as extra flour makes the buns dry and dense.
Roll the log tightly so the buns hold their spiral and don't unwind in the oven.
Brushing the hot buns with butter and sprinkling with sugar keeps the crust soft and lightly sweet.
variations: Add an extra 1/2 tsp ground cardamom to the cinnamon filling for a stronger Swedish flavour.
Skip the sugar topping and drizzle the cooled buns with a glaze of 1/2 cup icing sugar mixed with 1 tbsp milk.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 5–8 minutes, until warmed through.

title: Sri Lankan dhal curry
summary: Golden red lentils simmered in coconut milk with curry leaves, turmeric and toasted mustard seeds.
ingredients: 2 onions, 1 finely sliced and 1 finely chopped
2 green chillies, 1 slit lengthways and 1 finely chopped
method: Rinse the red lentils until the water runs almost clear. Put them in a medium saucepan with one chopped onion, the slit chilli, garlic, turmeric, 6 curry leaves and 750 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, skimming off any foam. Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 15–18 minutes until the lentils are soft and falling apart, then stir in the salt.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm over low heat for 4–5 minutes until hot and creamy, without boiling hard. Loosen with a splash of water if thicker than a loose porridge.
Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat. Cook the mustard seeds for 30–60 seconds until they pop.
Add the sliced onion and chopped chilli and cook for 4–5 minutes until golden. Add the remaining 6 curry leaves and cook 30 seconds until crisp.
Stir the tempering through the dhal and serve with lime wedges.

stages.title: Rinse and prepare
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs almost clear, then drain.
Finely slice 1 onion and finely chop the other onion.
Slit 1 green chilli lengthways and finely chop the second one.
Finely chop the garlic and cut the lime into wedges.

stages.title: Simmer the lentils
steps: Put the lentils, chopped onion, slit chilli, garlic, turmeric, half the curry leaves (6 leaves) and 750 ml water in a medium saucepan.
Bring to the boil over high heat, skimming off any foam.
Reduce to medium-low heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15–18 minutes until the lentils are soft and falling apart.
Stir in the salt.

stages.title: Add the coconut milk
steps: Pour in the coconut milk and stir well.
Warm over low heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until hot and creamy; do not let it boil hard.
Add a splash of water if the dhal is thicker than a loose porridge.

stages.title: Temper and serve
steps: Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the mustard seeds and cook for 30–60 seconds until they pop.
Add the sliced onion and chopped chilli and cook, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until golden.
Add the remaining 6 curry leaves and cook for 30 seconds until crisp and fragrant.
Pour the tempering over the dhal, stir through lightly and serve with lime wedges.

tips: Adding coconut milk after the lentils are soft stops it splitting and keeps the dhal creamy.
Fry the curry leaves last and briefly, as they turn bitter if they brown too much.
Salt added once the lentils are soft prevents the skins from toughening.
variations: Stir 100 g baby spinach through with the coconut milk and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes to the tempering oil for a hotter dhal.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

title: Lemon chicken orzo
summary: Tender chicken and orzo simmered in lemony broth with oregano, spinach and a silky finish.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh, boneless and skinless
method: Zest and juice the lemon separately, dice the onion and crush the garlic. Toss the chicken thighs with the oregano, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large deep lidded frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken 4–5 minutes per side until deeply golden, then set aside.
Reduce to medium, add the remaining oil and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and zest for 30 seconds, then the orzo for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and remaining salt, scraping up the browned bits, and bring to a simmer. Nestle the chicken back in with its juices.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–14 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the chicken has no pink in the centre. Rest the chicken for 5 minutes.
Stir the spinach and lemon juice through the orzo over low heat for 1–2 minutes until wilted and saucy. Slice the chicken, serve on top and season to taste.

stages.title: Prepare the chicken and aromatics
steps: Finely zest the lemon, then juice it, keeping the zest and juice separate.
Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic.
Trim any excess fat from the chicken thighs and pat them dry with paper towel.
Toss the chicken with the oregano, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep frying pan with a lid over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken and cook for 4–5 minutes per side, until deeply golden. It will not be cooked through yet.
Transfer the chicken to a plate.

stages.title: Cook the orzo
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan, then cook the onion for 4 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and lemon zest and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the orzo and stir for 1 minute to coat it in the oil.
Pour in the chicken stock and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pan, and bring to a simmer.

Nestle the chicken back into the pan along with any juices on the plate, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–14 minutes, stirring the orzo gently once or twice, until the orzo is tender and the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the centre.

stages.title: Finish and rest
steps: Move the chicken to a board and rest it for 5 minutes.
Stir the baby spinach and the lemon juice through the orzo over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the orzo is creamy and saucy.
Slice the chicken, return it to the pan or serve it on top, and taste for salt and pepper.

tips: Browning the chicken first builds a savoury base in the pan, which flavours the stock the orzo absorbs.
Add the lemon juice at the end because long cooking dulls its brightness and can turn it bitter.
Stir the orzo only gently and rarely, as constant stirring releases starch and can make it gluey rather than creamy.
Resting the chicken keeps the juices in the meat so slices stay moist.
variations: Stir through 100 g crumbled feta and a handful of chopped dill just before serving.
Add 1 cup of halved kalamata olives with the spinach for a saltier, more briny finish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The orzo will thicken, so reheat with a splash of water or stock until steaming hot throughout. Not suitable to freeze.

title: Chicken momo
summary: Steamed dumplings packed with ginger-scented chicken, spring onion and coriander.
method: Mix the flour and half the salt with the water, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth and firm. Cover with a damp tea towel and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the chicken mince, spring onions, ginger, garlic, onion, coriander, soy sauce, cumin, pepper, remaining salt and oil by hand until sticky and well combined.
Divide the dough into 24 pieces and roll each into a thin 9 cm circle, with the edges thinner than the centre.
Put 1 tablespoon of filling in each circle, then pleat and pinch the edge to seal fully, twisting the top closed.
Bring water to the boil in a wok or pot over high heat. Arrange the momo in a lined or oiled steamer, 2 cm apart, and set it over the water on medium-high.
Steam in batches for 12–15 minutes, until the dough is translucent and the chicken is cooked through with no pink remaining. Serve hot.

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl.
Add 180 ml water gradually, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 8 minutes until smooth and firm.
Cover the dough with a damp tea towel and rest for 30 minutes.

stages.title: Mix the filling
steps: Place the chicken mince in a bowl with the spring onions, ginger, garlic, onion and coriander.
Add the soy sauce, cumin, black pepper, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and the oil.
Mix with your hands for 2 minutes until the filling looks sticky and well combined.

stages.title: Roll and fill the momo
steps: Divide the dough into 24 equal pieces and cover them with the damp tea towel.
Roll each piece on a lightly floured bench into a thin 9 cm circle, keeping the edges thinner than the centre.
Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the middle of a circle.
Pleat the edge around the filling, pinching to seal fully and twisting the top closed.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

stages.title: Steam the momo
steps: Line a bamboo steamer with baking paper punched with holes, or lightly oil it, and bring water in a wok or pot to a boil over high heat.
Arrange a batch of momo in the steamer with 2 cm between them, then place the steamer over the boiling water and reduce to medium-high heat.
Steam each batch for 12–15 minutes, until the dough is translucent and the chicken is cooked through with no pink remaining.
Serve straight away while hot.

tips: Roll the edges of each circle thinner than the centre so the pleated top isn't doughy and the base can hold the filling without tearing.
Keep unused dough pieces under a damp tea towel because dry dough cracks and won't seal.
Finely chopped onion in the filling releases moisture as it steams, which keeps the lean chicken mince juicy.
Oil or line the steamer so the momo don't stick to it and tear their bases.
variations: Serve with a tomato chilli achar made from blended tomatoes, chilli, garlic and coriander.
Pan-fry the steamed momo in a little oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until the bases are golden.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze uncooked on a tray, then bag, for up to 2 months. Re-steam for 8–10 minutes (15 minutes from frozen) until steaming hot throughout.

title: Arepas con queso
summary: Golden corn cakes with crisp edges and a soft, cheesy centre.
method: Whisk the cornmeal and salt in a large bowl. Mix in the warm water and 15 g of the butter by hand, then knead 2 minutes until soft and smooth.
Cover and rest the dough for 5 minutes. Knead in the grated mozzarella for 2 minutes until evenly distributed.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide, pinching any cracks smooth.
Melt half the remaining butter in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook 4 arepas for 7 minutes until golden, then flip and cook 6 minutes more until golden and hollow-sounding.
Wipe the pan, melt the last of the butter over medium heat and cook the other 4 arepas the same way, 7 minutes then 6 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding. Serve hot.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Whisk the cornmeal and salt together in a large bowl.
Pour in 300 ml warm water and 15 g of the butter, then mix with your hands until no dry patches remain.
Knead for 2 minutes until the dough is soft, smooth and doesn't stick to your hands. Add a little more cornmeal if it is sticky, or a splash of water if it cracks.

stages.title: Rest and add the cheese
steps: Cover the bowl with a clean tea towel and rest the dough for 5 minutes so the cornmeal absorbs the water.
Add the grated mozzarella and knead for 2 minutes until the cheese is evenly distributed through the dough.

stages.title: Shape the arepas
steps: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Flatten each ball between your palms into a disc about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide.
Pinch and smooth any cracks around the edges so the discs don't split while cooking.

stages.title: Cook the arepas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and melt half the remaining butter (about 7 g).
Cook 4 arepas for 7 minutes on the first side, until a golden crust forms and they release easily from the pan.
Flip and cook for another 6 minutes, until golden on both sides, the cheese has melted and they sound hollow when tapped.

Transfer to a plate and wipe out the pan with paper towel. Return it to medium heat, melt the last of the butter and cook the remaining 4 arepas the same way, 7 minutes on the first side and 6 minutes on the second, until golden and hollow-sounding. Serve hot.

tips: Use precooked masarepa, not ordinary cornmeal or polenta, which will not form a dough.
Resting the dough lets the cornmeal hydrate fully, which stops the edges cracking when you shape the discs.
Medium heat cooks the arepas through and melts the cheese; high heat browns the outside before the centre is hot.
Coarsely grated mozzarella gives pockets of melted, stretchy cheese rather than a uniform dough.
variations: Split the hot arepas and fill with scrambled eggs.
Use half mozzarella and half grated feta for a saltier, tangier filling, and reduce the salt to 1/2 tsp.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side until hot through.

title: French lentil salad with goat cheese
summary: Peppery green lentils tossed with mustard vinaigrette, herbs and creamy goat cheese.
ingredients: 1 bunch parsley, leaves picked and roughly chopped
method: Rinse the lentils and simmer with the bay leaf in 750 ml water over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape.
Drain the lentils, discard the bay leaf and let them steam dry for 2 minutes.
Soak the diced shallots in the red wine vinegar for 5 minutes, then whisk in the mustard, olive oil, salt and pepper until thick.
Toss the warm lentils through the dressing and leave for 5 minutes.
Fold through the chopped parsley and adjust the salt or vinegar to taste.
Divide among 4 bowls and top with the crumbled goat cheese.

stages.title: Cook the lentils
steps: Rinse the lentils under cold water and drain, then place them in a medium saucepan with the bay leaf.
Add 750 ml water and bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low heat.
Simmer, partly covered, for 20–25 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Drain well in a sieve, discard the bay leaf and let the lentils steam dry for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Finely dice the shallots and place them in a large bowl with the red wine vinegar.
Leave for 5 minutes to soften and mellow the raw bite.
Whisk in the dijon mustard, olive oil, salt and black pepper until the dressing is thick and combined.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add the warm lentils to the dressing and toss to coat evenly.
Leave for 5 minutes so the lentils absorb the dressing.
Chop the parsley leaves and fold them through the lentils.
Taste and add a little more salt or vinegar if needed, then divide among 4 bowls and top with the crumbled goat cheese.

tips: Dress the lentils while they are still warm, because they absorb the vinegar and oil far better than cold lentils.
Salt the cooking water only at the end, as adding it early can toughen the lentil skins.
Soaking the shallots in the vinegar softens their sharpness so the salad tastes balanced rather than harsh.
Green or French-style lentils hold their shape; red lentils would collapse into mush.
variations: Add 2 roasted, diced beetroot and a handful of rocket for an earthy, peppery version.
Replace the goat cheese with crumbled feta and add a handful of chopped walnuts for crunch.
storage: Refrigerate the lentils and dressing, without the cheese, in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Serve cold or at room temperature and add the goat cheese just before eating.
